name: Robert Delaunay
bio: Robert Delaunay was a French artist of the School of Paris movement who, with his wife Sonia Delaunay and others, co-founded the Orphism art movement, noted for its use of strong colours and geometric shapes. His later works were more abstract. His work includes the bold use of color, and shows his clear love of experimentation with both depth and tone.

paintings.title: Rhythms (Delaunay)
paintings.story: Rhythms is an oil on canvas painting by the French artist Robert Delaunay, from 1934. It is part of the collection of the Musée National d'Art Moderne, in Paris.

paintings.title: Champs de Mars: The Red Tower
paintings.story: Champs de Mars: The Red Tower is an oil on canvas painting by the French painter Robert Delaunay, from 1911. It shows an orphic representation of the Eiffel Tower, in Paris. The painting is held in the Art Institute of Chicago.
facts: Delaunay's painting style changed quickly in the first decade of the 20th century, keeping pace with the artistic developments of the time.
Only few years before of the current painting, he still followed the neo-impressionist style.

paintings.title: Still Life with a Parrot
paintings.story: Still Life with a Parrot is an oil painting on canvas by the French artist Robert Delaunay, from 1907. It is held in the Unterlinden Museum, in Colmar, Alsace.
facts: The Colmar painting is a manifestation of the young artist's interest in Michel-Eugène Chevreul's theories on colours, and one of his first experimental works.
The painting had belonged to the art dealer Louis Carré (1897–1977) and was bought after his death by the Société Schongauer which administrates the museum since its foundation.

paintings.title: Portuguese Woman
paintings.story: Portuguese Woman, also known as Tall Portuguese Woman, is an oil and wax on canvas painting by the French painter Robert Delaunay, created in 1916. It is held in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, in Madrid. There are others similarly named paintings by the same artist from this phase, in other museums.
facts: Robert and Sonia Delaunay where at the resort of San Sebastián, in Spain, when the First World War overtook them by surprise.
They decided to move to Portugal, settling in the northern village of Vila do Conde, near Porto, where they lived from June 1915 to March 1916.

paintings.title: Homage to Blériot
paintings.story: Homage to Blériot is a tempera on canvas painting by French painter Robert Delaunay, from 1914. It is held at the Kunstmuseum Basel. Another version of the same painting is held at the Museum of Grenoble. These paintings belong to the series Disks.
facts: The Disks series was inspired by the colour theory of French chemist Michel Eugène Chevreul, and the concept of the simultaneous contrasts of colours.

This canvas celebrates the French aviation pioneer and constructor Louis Blériot, in a typical simultaneist composition, by notably representing symbols of progress, namely a biplane, seen flying above the Eiffel Tower, in Paris, at the right, and a propeller, at the left.

paintings.title: Windows Open Simultaneously 1st Part, 3rd Motif
paintings.story: Windows Open Simultaneously 1st Part, 3rd Motif is an oil-on-canvas painting by French painter Robert Delaunay, created in 1912. It is part of the Windows painting series. The current painting, like its predecessor, Simultaneous Windows 2nd Motif, 1st Part, is held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, in New York. A painting with the same title is held at Tate Modern, in London.
facts: The artist had been inspired by analytic cubism in his geometric forms, but this orphic composition is defined by the usage or diaphanous and prismatic colours.
Delaunay when he created this painting series had already left representation.

paintings.title: Portrait of Tristan Tzara
paintings.story: Portrait of Tristan Tzara is an oil on paperboard painting by the French painter Robert Delaunay, created in 1923. It depicts the Romanian poet Tristan Tzara, a leading name of the Dada movement and a personal friend of the artists couple Robert and Sonia Delaunay. It is held in the Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía, in Madrid.
facts: The most striking element of the painting isn't the poet's thoughtful face, but the orange scarf he wears, which is in the center of the painting and occupies the largest space.
During the First World War, Robert and Sonia Delaunay took refuge in Spain and Portugal, where they continued their artistic work on the observation of light and colors.
